option_title: Fine-tuning steps against policy success in simulation
question: Does simulated success keep rising as fine-tuning grows from 2,000 to 32,000 steps on a fixed dataset?
hypothesis: Success levels off near 8,000 steps, because the fixed dataset, not training compute, limits what the policy can learn.

predictions.if_lever: Success at 32,000 steps beats success at 8,000 steps by more than 5 points.
predictions.if_not: Success at 32,000 steps is within 2 points of success at 8,000 steps across 3 seeds.
predictions.decision_rule: Compute is the lever if success(32k) - success(8k) > 5 points and exceeds twice the seed spread.
predictions.noise_rule: Three training seeds per level; a difference counts only if it exceeds twice the spread across seeds.
predictions.expected_why: Published fine-tuning curves on small datasets flatten early.

compute_tested_why: Training steps are bought with GPU hours.
scored_against: The simulator's own success flag for each episode.

anchor.what: Reproduce the released checkpoint's success rate of 31% within 3 points [s2].

checks: reproduce the released success rate before the sweep

phases.stop_rule: stop if reproduction misses by more than 3 points

numbers.name: training steps per instance-hour
numbers.quote: about 5,000 steps per hour on one 8-GPU H100 node
numbers.page_setting: a larger policy on a different dataset

numbers.name: training steps in the sweep (3 seeds per level)

restructuring.sequential_part: Each fine-tuning step waits on the weights the step before produced.

novelty.closest_prior: A published fine-tuning study trained up to 20,000 steps and reported success still rising at that point [s3].
novelty.left_open: Whether success keeps rising beyond 20,000 steps when the dataset is held fixed.

test_summary: Fine-tune the same policy for 2,000, 8,000 and 32,000 steps, three seeds each. Compare simulated success at each level with the released checkpoint [s2].

sources.quote: about 5,000 steps per hour on one 8-GPU H100 node
The released checkpoint reaches a 31% success rate.
